title: REQ-20261106-OPS002 — Travel notice on file & verified pre-change contact details for call-back (Grace Williams)
content:
Member record extract for Grace Williams (DOB 22/07/1963, age 63; Williamstown VIC 3016), Caldova Super (Select) CS-1058220, balance $612,400. Grace is a direct member — no adviser is linked to the account, so all contact is with Grace herself. Prepared for Financial Crime and Client Communications to decide how — and through which channel — Grace can be contacted safely.

Travel notice (on file): lodged 12 Oct 2026 by secure message from Grace's usual online session (registered iPad, Melbourne IP, MFA to her verified mobile). It reads: travelling through Italy from 18 Oct 2026 (departing Melbourne Airport), returning 4 Dec 2026; 'I won't be making any changes to my account while I'm away — please email me if anything comes up.' Preferred contact while travelling: email.

Verified contact details held BEFORE 2 Nov 2026 — the trusted channels for any call-back: mobile 0491 570 157 (verified, used for MFA for several years); email grace.williams@example.com (verified, used for all statements); residential address in Williamstown (unchanged).

Details changed on 2 Nov 2026 by an unverified phone caller — NOT trusted until Grace confirms them through a verified channel: mobile 0491 570 158; email grace.w.super@mailbox.example.

Why it matters: the travel notice and the pre-change details are the trusted reference points for this case. The 3 Nov login from a new device in Sydney and the 6 Nov full-balance rollover request are inconsistent with a member who told us she is in Italy and would make no changes. Caldova's controls require any verification call-back to use the details held before the change — never a number or email supplied by the person making the request — and require MFA codes to go to a verified number.

Handling notes: Grace may be hard to reach because of time-zone differences (Italy is 10 hours behind Melbourne in November); email her previous verified address and call the previous verified mobile. Treat her as a likely victim of identity takeover: be clear, calm and reassuring, never imply she did anything wrong, and do not discuss any suspicious matter report.
